ios.desc:
Your smart, fast Hacker News reader, powered by AI.

Hack The News turns Hacker News into a clean native reading experience for developers, founders, startup people, and curious tech readers. Browse top, best, new, show, ask, and job stories. Open discussions without clutter. Get instant AI summaries when an article is too long and you just need the key points.

Why Hack The News?
- AI summaries: get a TLDR for any story and decide what is worth reading.
- Native reader: read articles, comments, and link previews in a fast iPhone-first interface.
- Search: find stories, comments, and users across all of Hacker News.
- Translation: translate stories, comments, and summaries into your preferred language.
- Bookmarks: save articles, developer news, startup ideas, and YC job posts for later.
- Jobs board: browse Hacker News and YC startup jobs directly in the app.
- Widgets: keep top tech stories on your Home Screen.
- Custom themes: tune the reading experience to match your style.

Premium unlocks the full experience:
- Unlimited AI summaries
- Unlimited bookmarks
- Full theme customization
- Home Screen widgets
- All future premium features included

Built for the Hacker News community. No ads. No clutter. Just the stories, links, comments, and software news that matter.

Download Hack The News and read Hacker News smarter, not longer.

Terms of Use (EULA): https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/dev/stdeula/

quotes.text:
Hey HN!

I've been maintaining HackTheNews (a native iOS client for Hacker News) for a while now, and with iOS 26 dropping its new "Liquid Glass" design language, I couldn't resist doing a full visual overhaul.

What's new:
- Complete redesign using iOS 26's Liquid Glass materials
- Translucent, layered UI that adapts to your wallpaper
- New glass-style navigation and tab bars
- Refined typography and spacing for the new aesthetic

Implementation notes for fellow iOS devs:
- Used the new `.glassEffect()` modifiers throughout
- Had to rethink some hierarchy decisions – Liquid Glass works best with 
  fewer nested containers

The before/after difference is pretty striking. Happy to share more technical details if anyone's curious about adopting Liquid Glass in their own apps.

Would love to hear your feedback – especially from fellow HN readers on what features you'd like to see next. Always open to suggestions!

quotes.text:
Hack The News is a modern iOS client that combines Hacker News with AI capabilities to enhance the reading experience. Built with Swift and SwiftUI.

Key features:
- AI-powered article summaries and insights
- Native iOS experience
- Clean, modern UI
- Rich link previews
- Nested comment threading
- iOS widgets

The AI integration (using OpenAI) helps users:
- Get quick summaries of long articles
- Extract key insights and main points

I built this because I wanted to combine the intellectual depth of HN discussions with modern AI capabilities, while maintaining a clean, native iOS experience.

App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/hack-the-news-hacker-news-app/id6447095897

Looking forward to your feedback, especially on the AI integration!
